delivery_target: future consumer: callers of store_pde_global_objs can drop valid_global_refs from their own preconditions
new_lemma:
lemma store_pde_global_objs_no_global_refs[wp]:
  "\\<lbrace>valid_global_objs and
    valid_arch_state and
    (\\<lambda>s. (\\<forall>pd. (obj_at (empty_table (set (second_level_tables (arch_state s))))
                     (p \\<and>\\<and> \\<not>\\<not> mask pd_bits) s
             \\<and> ko_at (ArchObj (PageDirectory pd)) (p \\<and>\\<and> \\<not>\\<not> mask pd_bits) s
               \\<longrightarrow> empty_table (set (second_level_tables (arch_state s)))
                                   (ArchObj (PageDirectory (pd(ucast (p \\<and>\\<and> mask pd_bits >> 2) := pde)))))
          \\<or> (\\<exists>slot. cte_wp_at (\\<lambda>cap. p \\<and>\\<and> \\<not>\\<not> mask pd_bits \\<in> obj_refs cap) slot s))\\<rbrace>
     store_pde p pde \\<lbrace>\\<lambda>rv. valid_global_objs\\<rbrace>"
  apply (simp add: store_pde_def)
  apply wp
  apply clarsimp
  done
rationale: The proof of store_pde_global_objs is `apply (simp add: store_pde_def); apply wp; apply clarsimp; done` — extremely opaque, with NO conjunct visibly consumed. The `valid_global_refs` conjunct head never appears in the proof body and `wp; clarsimp` does not name it. Dropping it yields a strictly stronger Hoare triple. A trial build is the cheap ground truth.
strengthening_claim: (valid_global_objs and valid_arch_state and <lambda>) <= (valid_global_objs and valid_global_refs and valid_arch_state and <lambda>)
